newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat stable, ignores Egyptian contract.
newsitem.headline: French wheat stable, ignores Egyptian contract.

text.p: Wheat prices were stable on Monday as continued harvest pressure offset news of a large French wheat sale to Egypt, dealers said.
"It (the sale) is not enough to move prices," said one trader, adding that warehouses were currently running out of storage space for the incoming grain.
Rouen wheat for Aug-Sept delivery was quoted at 895-900 francs per tonne and at 890 francs for Sept-Dec delivery, unchanged from Friday.
Forecasts of sharply higher yields in northern France depressed prices last week with August wheat bottoming out at some 885 francs by mid-week.
On Saturday Egypt bought 200,000 tonnes of French wheat for October shipment at $178 a tonne fob, a level traders described as "very low".
They said the contract would be hard to cover unless the EU awarded export rebates through its weekly grain tenders system.
But member country officials said the Commission appeared reluctant to grant refunds on soft wheat until it gets a firmer crop picture.
